_note: Conversation scenes. Each plays after the expedition named in 'after', when every companion in 'cast' is in the party; otherwise the party goes straight to town. Lines are {"say": companion id or name, "text"} or {"narrate"}. A choice's 'next' names another node of the same scene; no 'next' returns to town. 'sameAs' copies another node's lines. Choices change companion approval only, never XP or loot.

night.title: The Night after the Bridge
night.objective: Sit with your companions after the bridge.

lines.narrate: The refugee camp below Ashford has gone quiet. Someone has lent your party a cooking pot, and Maren has used it. She hands you the first bowl.

lines.text: It has nourishment. Colours are a luxury of the well-provisioned.

lines.narrate: Nessa tips her bowl toward the dog that has followed the carts all the way from the bridge. The dog sniffs it, considers, and lies down facing the other way.

lines.text: He named himself. I just guessed right.

lines.narrate: Orin hasn't touched his bowl. He is scrubbing the lid of the borrowed pot, slowly and carefully, and the lid is already clean.

lines.text: Orin. That's the third time you've cleaned that.
Fourth. You weren't watching for the first one.

lines.narrate: The child from the last cart is asleep against a wheel twenty paces away, still wearing the blanket Orin gave her.

lines.text: She asked me if soldiers always leave first. On the bridge. I didn't have an answer.

lines.narrate: Orin is quiet for a long moment. Then he sets down the lid and picks up his bowl.

lines.text: Nice thing to say. Doesn't make it true for her.

choices.label: “Tell her the truth tomorrow. All of it.”

lines.text: All of it is a long story.
Then start with the short part.

lines.narrate: Nobody speaks. Maren looks at you as if you had kicked something. Then Orin nods, once, as if you have finally said something true.

lines.text: That is not what a frightened child needs to hear.
It's what I needed to hear.

choices.label: Say nothing and sit beside him

lines.narrate: You sit. The fire pops. After a while Nessa gets up without a word and slides her bowl across to Orin. Biscuit follows the bowl.

lines.text: He's yours now. The dog, not the stew. Well. Both.

lines.narrate: Later, when the fire is low, Orin eats the stew. All of it. Maren watches him do it and says nothing.

breakfast.title: Morning in the Camp
breakfast.objective: See what Orin does with the truth.

lines.narrate: Morning comes grey and cold. The child from the last cart is called Wenna, it turns out, and she finds Orin before he can find her.

lines.text: You're the one who gave me the blanket.
Do I have to give it back?

lines.narrate: She nods, satisfied, and waits. Orin crouches so his eyes are level with hers. It takes him a long time to get all the way down.

lines.text: You asked me if soldiers always leave first. Sometimes they do. I did, once. A long time ago, at a place a lot like that bridge.

lines.narrate: Wenna considers this with great seriousness.

lines.text: Then you're getting better at it.

lines.narrate: She goes back to her mother with the blanket trailing in the mud. Orin stays crouched there until Maren offers him a hand up, and for once he takes it.

lines.text: It was also the truest thing I have heard you say in a year.
